newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Market growth to boost Vodafone.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Market growth to boost Vodafone.

text.p: Vodafone Group, Britain's biggest mobile phones company, is expected on Tuesday to report a healthy rise in first half pretax profits on the back of a pick-up in the UK market, analysts say.
Analysts have pencilled in pretax profits at around 230 million pounds before a 10 million pound exceptional credit, against 208 million pounds last time.
Dividends are forecast in a tight 2.26-2.36p range compared to 1.97p in the first half of 1995.

Losses at Vodafone's stakes in overseas networks, at 17 million stg last time, are expected to be cut back sharply to a 3-10 million stg loss, with some analysts forecasting breakeven before the full year stage.
Some analysts also expect Vodafone to present plans next weel for a new fixed network replacement product for corporates.

Vodafone's shares, which closed up 3p at 239.5p on Friday, may be undervalued in the face of an acceleration in the UK mobile phone market and its new market range, some analysts say, although the group faces stiffer competition from rivals like Orange and Cable and Wireless' Mercury One-2-One.
Vodafone also faces the cost of customers who stop using its older analogue network and move over to the new digital system.

Vodafone's "churn" level, the number of cancelled subscriptions, could fall to 24 percent from 25 percent -- compared to Orange's 18 percent and BT's majority-owned Cellnet unit at around 30 percent, according to ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Telecoms analyst Jim McCafferty at the brokers puts Orange's lower churn level down to the high price the company charges for handsets, resulting in a "better quality" of subscriber.

At the end of September 1996, Vodafone had a total subscriber base of more than 2.66 million which included more than 1.6 million on its analogue network. -- Kirstin Ridley, London newsroom +44 171 542 7987
